requirements.evidence: Repository source and documentation; static inspection only; tests and live services not run
requirements.requirement: Provide independently installable read-only MCP connectors in a Python 3.12+ uv workspace, shared mcp-core runtime, cross-market comparison, shortlist inspection and a unified marketplace server. Support stdio and configured HTTP serving. Source availability depends on upstream shape, network and operator browser session; documentation is not a live availability guarantee.
requirements.rule: Read catalog, listing, review, seller and optional analytics data only. Do not place orders, publish reviews or mutate marketplace accounts. Local caching, diagnostics and operator browser lifecycle are separate from marketplace writes. POST used for read-only upstream queries does not imply an account-writing capability.

Public marketplace connectors must not require stored marketplace API credentials: use anonymous access or the operator's existing Chrome session. Preserve the documented optional MPStats exception: MPSTATS_MP_AUTH supplies a paid account token, and absence returns auth_missing without disabling other sources. MCP HTTP authentication tokens protect the server deployment, not marketplace access. Do not expose token values in logs, errors or responses. Taobao and Megamarket may require an already logged-in operator browser; do not promise anonymous access for them.

A missing or ambiguous value is None, never a fabricated zero. Use coerce_price and coerce_int rather than guessing. Do not turn an unavailable price into the cheapest offer; preserve price-kind and conditional-price distinctions. This rule does not prohibit genuine zero counts where the upstream contract establishes them.

When a reachable payload no longer matches the expected structure, report parser_drift. Distinguish format change from transport_down, rate limits, missing products, login walls and challenge_required. Selfchecks report success, drift_detected or inconclusive; a blocked probe does not verify parser health. Shape signatures retain paths and types, not payload values; adoption differs by connector.

Use ErrorCode: auth_missing, rate_limited, timeout, transport_down, parser_drift, bad_request, permission_denied, challenge_required, not_found. Only rate_limited, timeout, transport_down and challenge_required have retryable=true. ConnectorError serializes error, message and retryable plus applicable provider, retry_after_s and status_code; raise_tool_error wraps JSON in FastMCP ToolError. ChallengeRequiredError additionally describes required user action and optional handoff metadata.

Never write application diagnostics to stdout in MCP server code: stdio stdout belongs to JSON-RPC. Use log_event on stderr or FastMCP Context logging. Operator cli.py and __main__ entrypoints are excluded by the no-print guard; their human-facing output is not an MCP server diagnostic channel.

rule.source: CONTRIBUTING.md; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:Untrusted output,Input validation over escaping; packages/mcp-core/src/mcp_core/transport/chrome_cdp.py

requirements.rule: Validate IDs, slugs, URL paths and filter inputs against the supported shapes before upstream access. Treat seller/buyer text as untrusted data, not instructions. Preserve CDP origin/redirect guards and use the operator-owned browser rather than storing session credentials or solving captchas automatically.

Keep request pacing, bounded response bodies, bounded retries and browser concurrency budgets. The shared HTTP tier retries transport failures and 502/503/504, not 429 or other 4xx; redirects are disabled by default. Connector-specific tiers may differ. Do not remove politeness gaps, substitute captcha-solving services or implement nonexistent upstream capabilities; Detsky Mir deliberately has no text-search tool.

Ordinary tests must run offline by replacing upstream fetches and asserting error codes, warnings and response fields. Network tests use live and browser tests use cdp; the offline CI suite excludes both. The nightly/manual live job is separate and covers only sources with live-marked tests. A file named parser_live may instead exercise captured fixtures offline; inspect markers and assertions rather than infer coverage from its name.

Use captured, trimmed real HTML/SSR fixtures rather than invented upstream markup; retain .provenance.json evidence and SHA-256 pins for captured fixtures. check_provenance verifies existing top-level HTML/JSON fixture pairs with declared pins, accepting raw/LF/CRLF hashes and dated known-stale exceptions; its current exception map is empty. It does not enforce that every fixture has provenance or reject all malformed/missing sidecars, so fixture completeness remains a review responsibility.

rule.source: scripts/version_sites.py; scripts/check_versions.py; scripts/bump_version.py; pyproject.toml; packages/*/pyproject.toml; packages/*/src/*/__init__.py; packages/*/src/*/server.py; docker-compose.yml; docs/DEPLOYMENT.md; server.json; dsh/package.json

requirements.rule: One release carries one version, rooted in pyproject.toml. The current gate families contain 88 declarations: 17 project manifests, 16 package __version__ strings, 15 SERVER_VERSION constants, 19 compose/deployment/DSH README image tags, 3 deployment-guide release pins, 15 mcp-core pins, one registry version, one registry OCI image tag and one dsh bundle version. Update all affected declarations together; missing required declarations are failures. The declaration families and patterns live once in scripts/version_sites.py, which both check_versions.py and bump_version.py use. This is a static declaration count, not an executed release gate; the count may change with repository structure.

Do not silently rename, remove or retype tools, arguments or response fields. The committed public-contract snapshot pins mounted tool structure while excluding prose descriptions/titles, but keeps domain fields with those names. Regenerate only for an intentional owner-approved contract change. Response models that rename a field by alias (the _meta block) set serialize_by_alias so FastMCP 4 advertises and returns the alias, not the Python name. Preserve per-tool field descriptions and schema budgets; CI gates compare-mcp, decision-mcp and marketplace-mcp wire-token growth at 10 percent over the stored baseline. Operator selfchecks are not advertised as MCP tools.

Support Windows, Linux and macOS. Keep platform-specific process termination behind patchable seams, obtain POSIX-only functions through guarded getattr access and allowlist child environments. CI declares Python 3.12/3.13 on all three OSes and host/win32/darwin type checks; current execution outcomes are not verified by this documentation change.
requirements.requirement: Encode spaces in every Taobao search URL as %20, not +, including selfchecks. The same canonical URL remains the search cache and browser-handoff key; literal plus signs remain escaped query data.

requirement.source: Owner brief-taobao.md, 2026-10-30, issue 2 and owner decision dated 2026-10-30

requirements.requirement: Include ordinary detail.tmall.com/item.htm listings in Taobao search with their real HTTPS host, id, title, CNY price and shop, preserving item.taobao.com tiles. Deliberately exclude click.simba.taobao.com ad-click trackers because visiting them bills advertisers. Prove extraction offline against a trimmed real 2026-10-30 capture with at least two Taobao tiles, two Tmall tiles and one ad tile, source-derived ground truth and a SHA-256 provenance pin.

Refuse a detail.tmall.com card URL, or a Taobao card navigation rejected for redirecting there, with a clear non-retryable bad_request or not_found error. Say Tmall listings are not readable by taobao_card and search already carries title, price, shop and URL. Do not widen the CDP host policy or mine unrelated hosts for item ids.

Transport a structural boolean grid_loading from rendered text containing 加载中, excluding scripts/styles. For an empty grid with no login-wall or anti-bot markers, re-evaluate in the same owned page about every 1.5 seconds for at most about 10 extra seconds. Persistent loading is a retryable timeout, including the compare source outcome, not parser_drift. Login/CAPTCHA walls never wait and remain challenge_required; a non-loading empty grid remains parser_drift. Selfchecks must not call an unfinished grid parser drift. The marker is part of the search shape reference and a required key family, so losing it is loud. A page that offers login/register routes (login_anchors > 0) is never a loading grid, whatever its link count: it is not polled and with zero items stays parser_drift unless a wall marker fires (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

With WB_TRANSPORT=dom, preserve the card/search_v9 check keys and R.selfcheck_entry shape while calling dom_transport.render exactly once per subcheck with the tools' URL, extractor and parser. Never request card.wb.ru or search.wb.ru in DOM mode. Each entry carries transport=dom and the baseline SKU/query; bound and redact notes. A named, positively priced card and identified, positively priced search products are healthy. A missing named card or missing search anchors/prices is drift/schema_drift; an unavailable/unpriced main card offer or WB's own empty-result notice is inconclusive/baseline_gone. Decode render ToolError JSON by mcp_core.errors.ErrorCode: challenge_required is inconclusive/blocked, transport_down is inconclusive/transport_down, parser_drift is drift/schema_drift, the subcheck wall-clock timeout is inconclusive/timeout and unexpected errors are inconclusive/dependency_unavailable. Do not solve/retry a captcha or challenge. The DOM subcheck bound must cover the transport's own page waits. API-mode behavior and reviews/root_basket probes stay unchanged; search_goods keeps its probe/verdict and adds a note that wb_search does not use it in DOM mode. Document doctor's two rendered pages and error mapping. No live or marketplace network verification is authorized by this task.

In WB_TRANSPORT=api mode, when wb_card or wb_search gets an outright refusal from WB's API — HTTP 401, 403 or 498, or the edge's HTML wall page instead of JSON — and WB_DOM_FALLBACK is on (default on), re-read the same request through that tool's DOM path without changing any other response field, and add "dom_fallback: WB API refused this address (<reason>); read through the scraping Chrome" to meta.warnings. A 429, network error or timeout, parser drift and bad request are not fallbacks. Make one API attempt under the existing retry policy and at most one DOM attempt; if the DOM path fails too, preserve its error type and add that the API refused first to its message. Log "<tool>.dom_fallback" once per call with the reason. WB_DOM_FALLBACK=0 restores the exact API-only behaviour; WB_TRANSPORT=dom is unchanged. One classification helper is shared by both tools; other WB tools are untouched. doctor explains the automatic fallback when it is on and keeps the WB_TRANSPORT=dom instruction when it is off. No live or marketplace network verification is authorized. A rendered search tile whose prices keep unproven roles is returned with price_rub null and in_stock false next to the parser's warning; it never fails the whole page (pre-release audit A1, 2026-10-30). The dom_fallback warning also says prices and delivery follow the WB region set in the scraping browser rather than dest, for the default dest too (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

For a source in FOREIGN_CURRENCY_SOURCES, source_outcomes detail counts offers with price_native: N results, M priced in CUR (not ranked), using uppercase currency codes from the priced offers, sorted and joined with /. If M is zero, report N results, 0 priced (not ranked) without a currency. Other sources retain N results, M priced using price_rub. Do not change the priced ranking list, convert currencies or let foreign offers enter RUB ranking. Update foreign-currency explanations in README/docs/skills and prove 20 CNY-priced offers, missing native prices, mixed codes, unchanged RUB detail and unchanged ranking offline.

scripts/gen_tools_doc.py imports the compare, decision and full servers, calls their public list_tools after output-schema compaction, and generates docs/TOOLS.md: a generated-file header with the regeneration command; a profile table (profile, console script, tool count, tools/list UTF-8 bytes and approximate tokens marked ≈ from the one estimate scripts/mcp_wire.py and the dsh bundle gate share (mcp_wire.wire_tokens: per tool compact JSON, Cyrillic 1/3, other characters 1/4)); and, per profile and per tool-name prefix, one row per tool with its input parameters rendered from the JSON schema (name: type, = default when not required) and the first description paragraph. Output is deterministic: sorted, no timestamps or absolute paths, LF, identical on Windows and Linux. --check regenerates in memory and exits 1 with "docs/TOOLS.md is stale; run scripts/gen_tools_doc.py" when docs/TOOLS.md differs; the same measurement feeds the marked tools-cost block in the README's English and Russian tools sections, which the generator rewrites and --check verifies. One CI step in the unchanged lint job runs the check. Offline tests cover determinism, one row per tool, fresh/stale check behavior on temporary copies, README block rewriting, and required/default/enum/array parameter rendering. The same measurement also rewrites the marked mode table in dsh/README.md (tools-cost-dsh block), so no hand-typed per-profile token number remains in README.md, dsh/README.md or dsh/cordis.patch.yml.

requirements.requirement: install defaults to one marketplace entry running the selected profile's console script (compare by default; see R-CLI-INSTALL-PROFILE); --per-source preserves the source keys/scripts without changing the unified server's mounted sources. Resolve checkout uv and installed console scripts to absolute paths when found; warn once on stderr when uv is absent. --write supports platform-specific Claude Desktop and Cursor JSON files: reject malformed/non-object JSON and conflicting entries with exit 2, preserve unrelated entries/settings, create absent parents/files, back up existing bytes to file.bak-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS before changes (if the backup fails, exit 3 and change nothing), and replace atomically through a same-directory temporary file. An identical entry prints already configured, writes nothing and creates no backup; a conflicting entry needs --force; --dry-run with --write prints only the entries it would write, a replaces: line for an entry --force would replace, the names of the other servers and top-level settings it keeps (never their content: other servers' env blocks may hold keys; pre-release audit A3, 2026-10-30) and the target, without writes. A successful write prints the file path, the backup path and restart <client> to load it. claude-code --write prints exact claude mcp add commands only; dsh --write refuses while its existing patch emitter stays unchanged. Unknown clients/options fail with an explanation and exit 2. Prove behavior offline with temporary config paths. A config saved with a UTF-8 BOM is read; a config that is not UTF-8 (UTF-16, for example) exits 2 with a save-as-UTF-8 hint instead of a JSON error. A second write in the same second gets a -1, -2 ... backup name, so an earlier backup is never overwritten. A symlinked config is written through to its target and stays a symlink. claude-code without --write prints the claude mcp add lines first, then the project .mcp.json block under a comment that names it (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

install --profile compare|decision|full selects the console script of the one marketplace entry: compare-mcp (the default for new installs), decision-mcp or marketplace-mcp; the entry keeps the name marketplace. Generalize _unified_entry to take the script and resolve it exactly as before (absolute uv in a checkout, console script on PATH otherwise). --per-source keeps the per-source block and refuses a combination with --profile with exit 2. An unknown or missing profile exits 2 with the accepted values. Printed and --write output names the profile and says --profile full gives every per-source tool. A different existing marketplace entry still refuses without --force with exit 2 and changes nothing, and the refusal names the profile configured now and the profile asked for. --help mentions --profile. Prove offline with temporary config paths. Without an explicit --profile, install --write and setup keep the profile an existing marketplace entry already runs (recognized by its console script), so the compare default applies to new installs only; setup's dry run prints only the entry it would write, never the operator's other servers.

marketplace-mcp setup goes from zero to the first answer by reusing install, doctor, browser start and unblock, printing each step as it runs. Detect Claude Desktop (its config folder exists), Cursor (~/.cursor exists) and Claude Code (claude on PATH); a repeatable --client overrides detection; when none is found print the manual install commands and continue. Config uses install's write for Claude Desktop and Cursor with profile compare by default (--profile accepted) and prints the claude mcp add line for Claude Code without running it; a conflict is reported and skipped (setup has no --force; say how to force with install). Unless --no-browser call chrome_cdp.start_browser(visible=True), print a failure reason and continue. Unless --no-doctor say in one line that live requests follow, then run doctor's shared _run_selfchecks(None), _health_steps and _print_health_rows. When _blocked_sources finds a wall and stdin is a TTY, offer unblock with a y/N prompt and on yes call cmd_unblock(names); otherwise print the exact marketplace-mcp unblock <sources> command. Finish with Restart <client>, then the Russian iPhone 15 comparison ask. --dry-run prints the steps and files and writes, starts and requests nothing. Exit 0 when the config step succeeded for at least one client, 2 on bad arguments, 1 when nothing could be configured and no client was found. Touch only the client config files (plus backups) and the scraping Chrome. Prove offline with fakes and temporary config paths. Answering no to the unblock offer opens nothing and names the unblock command; Ctrl-C at the prompt prints cancelled and exits 130 before any page opens (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

Link docs/QUICKSTART.md. An unknown verb prints an explanation and usage and exits 2 without starting the server.

requirements.requirement: Preserve structured native selfcheck status and per-check reasons. A pure mapping uses those results and the static source capabilities, plus explicitly supplied CDP reachability and WB transport, to select one fixed next-step string for each non-success source. Print it below the source row and include next_step in each status-file source entry (null for success). Unreachable CDP advises the Chrome startup scripts or first-call autostart; browser walls advise `marketplace-mcp unblock <source>`, which opens the page a human passes and re-checks; WB card/search_v9 transport_down outside DOM mode advises the automatic DOM fallback when WB_DOM_FALLBACK is on and WB_TRANSPORT=dom when it is off; MPStats auth_missing advises MPSTATS_MP_AUTH in the server environment; drift advises diagnose_drift.py only for the sources that script accepts (citilink, dns, lamoda, taobao, megamarket) and otherwise advises a doctor run with --status-file plus an issue; a rate_limited check advises waiting 10-15 minutes and rerunning doctor, after the drift, auth and WB transport cases and before the CDP and wall cases; a selfcheck status of error means the check itself raised and advises opening an issue with its output, never the anti-bot advice; otherwise point to docs/ANTI_BOT.md. Never echo upstream advice or recommend captcha solvers, stealth/fingerprint tooling, proxy pools or retry loops. Map the real selfcheck codes, including Megamarket not_authenticated and Taobao login_wall, and verify offline.

requirements.requirement: The operator CLI gains browser status and browser show. Both work at the browser level over CDP: no owned page is needed and no page is ever navigated, so neither verb sends a request to any website. Status reports whether the CDP endpoint is reachable, the Chrome version, the number of page targets and whether the window is visible, off-screen (left or top at or below -10000) or minimized, and exits 0 when reachable and 1 when not. Show sets the first page target's window to windowState normal, then to on-screen bounds (left 80, top 40, keeping the current size when it is at least 800x600 and otherwise 1280x900), then activates that target, prints what it did, and exits 1 with the start hint when the endpoint is unreachable. The window-moving code is shared with reveal_owned_page rather than duplicated. The doctor next step for a browser-walled source names marketplace-mcp browser show instead of the launcher -Visible flag, and the usage screen lists both verbs. A failed CDP HTTP read of any kind (no answer, a broken HTTP exchange such as IncompleteRead, a body that is not JSON) reads as no answer and never escapes as an exception. Show minimizes an open window and then restores it: on Windows a background process cannot raise a window that sits behind others, and a restore does (checked on the owner's screen on 2026-10-30); an already minimized window is only restored.

requirement.source: Owner brief-dx2.md, 2026-10-30, DX wave 1 job 2, item 2; Owner brief-w2b-start-unblock.md, 2026-10-30, item 1

requirements.requirement: The Chrome launchers must not demand closing the everyday Chrome: Chrome allows a second instance with its own --user-data-dir. The launcher exits 0 with the port and how to show the window when the CDP endpoint already answers on the port, refuses with a clear message and exit 2 when another Chrome holds the same --user-data-dir, and otherwise starts Chrome even while other Chrome windows are open. The manual launch is on-screen by default (owner decision): the PowerShell script accepts -Hidden for the old off-screen launch and still accepts -Visible as a no-op; on macOS the shell hides the app only with --hidden. A hidden launch ends by pointing at marketplace-mcp browser show. The connector's own autostart stays off-screen. The PowerShell script stays ASCII without a BOM and parses in Windows PowerShell 5.1, the encoding trap that broke it in v2.5.2. With -AllowMainProfile the profile is Chrome's own User Data, which an everyday Chrome holds without naming it on its command line, so any running Chrome counts as holding it and the launcher refuses. The PowerShell launcher quotes --user-data-dir (Start-Process joins arguments with bare spaces), trims a trailing backslash, matches a running profile with an anchored, optionally quoted --user-data-dir pattern, waits about 12 s for CDP and exits 1 when it never answers. The shell launcher reports already running only when /json/version answers, refuses another listener on the port with exit 2, and anchors its pgrep pattern. The connector's Windows profile-PID lookup uses the same anchored pattern inside PowerShell and also covers msedge.exe (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

The operator CLI gains browser start [--hidden]. In chrome_cdp, start_browser(visible=True) reuses the autostart code: _start_chrome_with_cdp takes a stealth keyword (the autostart keeps today's call and therefore today's off-screen behaviour), and the port-bind wait is one helper shared by both. A visible start passes no off-screen arguments and does not hide the window; a hidden start behaves like the autostart, including CHROME_STEALTH=0 keeping it on-screen. If CDP already answers, start_browser returns started false and already_running true without spawning. A non-loopback CHROME_CDP_HOST is refused with a reason (the autostart rule). If the port never binds, the reason says another Chrome may hold the profile directory without remote debugging. The CLI exits 0 when CDP answers at the end (also when it already ran, then printing the browser show hint) and 1 with the reason otherwise, and the usage screen lists browser start. The scripts/start_chrome_cdp.ps1 and .sh changes are covered by R-CHROME-LAUNCHER. The report's off_screen is true only when the window was really parked (hidden, CHROME_STEALTH on, Windows, not headless); browser start prints the off-screen pointer only then and otherwise says --hidden parks the window only on Windows with CHROME_STEALTH on (pre-release audit A4, 2026-10-30).

A new module marketplace_connector/unblock.py holds the static UNBLOCK_PAGES map from every browser-backed doctor source (capabilities.browser_backed over the _SELFCHECKS table) to the page its search tool or browser selfcheck loads, or its login/home page when the wall is a login (Taobao login_wall, Megamarket not_authenticated); a test checks the map covers exactly those sources. marketplace-mcp unblock [sources...] [--wait SECONDS] [--dry-run]: named canonical sources that are not browser-backed exit 2 with "not a browser source; see marketplace-mcp doctor <source>"; with no names it runs the browser-backed selfchecks and takes those whose checks carry a WALL_REASONS reason, and prints and exits 0 when none is blocked. If CDP is unreachable it calls start_browser(visible=True) and exits 1 with its reason on failure. It opens each page in a new tab with browser-level Target.createTarget through chrome_cdp.open_tabs (which reports how many tabs opened before a failure instead of raising), never Page.navigate on an existing tab and never closes a tab, then raises the window and activates the first new tab through show_browser_window(target_id=...). It prints the page and the human action per source, then waits for Enter when stdin is a TTY or --wait seconds otherwise (default 180), re-runs only those sources' selfchecks and prints doctor's rows and next steps with doctor's exit codes (0 all ok, 1 drift, 2 still blocked). --dry-run prints the sources and pages, opens nothing and runs nothing else (without names it exits 2 because it would need live selfchecks). The output carries the budget line "Opens N page(s), one per source; the re-check makes the same requests as doctor." A human passes every check or login; nothing here solves, bypasses or automates a check. The doctor browser-wall next step names unblock and keeps the forbidden-words test passing. With no walled source the command says so and opens nothing; an unknown source name is refused, not opened; Ctrl-C at the Enter prompt prints cancelled and exits 130 before the recheck. open_tabs refuses a non-http(s) URL before the first CDP command, and the window is shown on the tab unblock just opened (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

requirement.source: Owner brief-dx2.md, 2026-10-30, DX wave 1 job 2, item 3

requirements.requirement: uv.lock must keep a revision of at least 5, the revision the Dockerfiles' uv 0.13.6 writes; uv 0.11.x rewrites it as revision 3. This is enforced by scripts/check_lock_revision.py in the style of the other check gates, not by a [tool.uv] required-version floor: that flag applies to every uv command and would stop an operator whose PATH carries an older uv from starting the server through the uv run --directory entry that install --write writes. The gate fails with the relock instruction (uvx --from uv==0.13.6 uv lock, or any uv >= 0.13.6) and is listed in CONTRIBUTING and docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md.

scripts/bump_version.py NEW [--dry-run] rewrites only the version text of every declaration (keeping the rest of the line, the file formatting and a JSON file's indentation and key order byte for byte), rejects NEW that is not X.Y.Z with an optional leading v with exit 2, and then runs the check_versions gate, exiting non-zero if it fails. --dry-run prints file:line old -> new and writes nothing. The declaration site table lives in scripts/version_sites.py and is the one definition both scripts use, so a site cannot be checked but not bumped or the reverse. After a successful bump the script prints the steps it does not do: relock with uvx --from uv==0.13.6 uv lock, move CHANGELOG [Unreleased] under [NEW] - date, and the release checklist. Offline tests on a copied mini-tree cover every site family, dry-run, exit 2, formatting, and the shared table. The site table also covers the docs/DEPLOYMENT.md release pins (the mcp_core wheel file name and the compare-connector[all] and aliexpress-connector specifiers): 88 declarations (pre-release audit, 2026-10-30).

.gitattributes declares * text=auto eol=lf and marks known binary artifact extensions binary, so every checkout matches the index on Windows as well as POSIX and scripts cannot arrive as CRLF. Adding it must change no blob in the index; the evidence is git ls-files --eol before and after plus the attempted renormalize check.

The tag-triggered workflows (release.yml, mcp-registry-publish.yml, pypi-publish.yml) run once per ref (concurrency group workflow-ref, cancel-in-progress false), check out with persist-credentials false and restore no cache (setup-uv enable-cache false, no cache-from). mcp-registry-publish downloads mcp-publisher v1.8.1 to a file, checks it against the pinned SHA-256 (GitHub's asset digest and registry_1.8.1_checksums.txt agree) and only then unpacks and runs it. CHROME_CDP_HOST may be an IPv6 literal, bare or bracketed: it is kept bare for dialing and the loopback test and bracketed in URLs (S1-F7).

.github/workflows/image-check.yml runs on workflow_dispatch and on pull requests touching Dockerfile, Dockerfile.stdio, uv.lock, pyproject.toml, packages/*/pyproject.toml or the workflow itself. It builds Dockerfile.stdio with docker/build-push-action loaded locally (push false), runs scripts/e2e_stdio_check_docker.py with MCP_DOCKER_IMAGE and MCP_EXPECTED_VERSION read from the root pyproject.toml, and builds Dockerfile without loading or pushing. Actions keep the exact SHAs pinned in the existing workflows, permissions are contents: read, and the concurrency group is event-aware. docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md tells the operator to run it on the release commit before tagging.

Any live run is bounded by at most 40 requests in total, at most 8 per marketplace and at least 3 seconds between two requests to one marketplace, read from LIVE_BUDGET_TOTAL, LIVE_BUDGET_PER_SOURCE and LIVE_BUDGET_GAP_S. scripts/live_budget.py keeps an in-memory ledger or the JSON file named by LIVE_BUDGET_LEDGER (atomic replace) so commands share one run, does not count loopback hosts, raises BudgetExhausted before an over-cap request is sent, and waits out the gap otherwise. install() hooks httpx AsyncClient/Client send, curl_cffi Session/AsyncSession request, chrome_cdp _playwright_page/_raw_cdp_page, in-page fetch evaluations on _RawCdpPage.evaluate and Playwright Page.evaluate, and ozon_connector.server._run_sync_bounded; a missing hook point raises AttributeError naming it. Every counted request prints one stderr line [req n/40] group n/8 kind url. The root conftest.py installs the budget once per session only when a selected test carries the live marker, and imports nothing for an offline selection. scripts/live_check.py offers selfcheck, call and ledger, always installs the budget and defaults the ledger to .live-budget.json in the repository root (gitignored). Offline tests with fake transports and a fake clock cover counting, both caps before sending, gap waits, loopback, the Ozon subprocess hook, a missing hook point, a ledger shared by two installs and the offline conftest path. A run ends explicitly: scripts/live_check.py reset archives the ledger under a timestamped name (never deletes it), and the over-cap message names that command. The chrome_cdp hooks also book a page.evaluate that calls window.open with a JSON string URL (http/https only) and every URL of open_tabs before the first tab opens. The ledger read-check-append-save runs under a lock file next to the ledger (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 50 ms retries, 10 s timeout as BudgetExhausted, a lock older than 60 s is stale), so two processes never lose a booking. scripts/live_check.py doctor runs the CLI doctor round under the budget and prints the ledger; the release checklist's go/no-go uses it.
